newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Crude demand may offset imports in APIs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Crude demand may offset imports in APIs.

text.p: REUTER SURVEY ESTIMATES* ACTUAL STOCKS FOR
UTILIZATION... UNCH/DOWN 1.0 pct 96.9 PCT UP 2.4 PCT PT
*NB - The survey estimate is derived by omitting the high and the low forecast and averaging the rest.
Crude oil stocks are expected to fall by about 2.5 million barrels in this week's report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) as strength in refinery demand offsets a rise in foreign imports.
A survey of estimates from traders and analysts found many still shaking their heads at last week's data, which showed suprising ouput combined with a jump in capacity utilization.

"Even though I think imports up coming a little from last week, if you assume nearly the same kind of run rate and some reconciliation of the (prior) data, you have to assume some kind of draw," said William Brown, president of WH Brown & Co.

Brown was referring to the API's previous crude data, which showed stocks building by nearly seven million barrels to 322.6 million barrels, but which apparently understated imports significantly, sources have said.
Regarding this week's report, others, like Brown, cited strong demand for WTI domestic crude would offset a perceive rise in imports.
Less clear was the outlook for gasoline stocks, with estimates ranging from a rise of 1.0 million barrels to a draw of 2.0 million.

"Gas is the one I'm most uncertain about. If output comes down, this could be a draw. The implied demand should snap back from last week's level, but given the refinery runs, I don't know if the demand rebound will be strong enough to prevent the build," Brown said.

Some sources were still concerned that gasoline stocks about the fact that gasoline stocks of 197 million barrels are nearly six million barrels below year-ago levels just days ahead of the three-day U.S. Memorial Day Weekend, the traditional start of the summer driving season.
Utilization rates were seen unchanged to down 1.0 percent from last week's strong, 2.4-percent rise to about 97 percent, with sources noting they simply cannot get much higher.
Distillate stocks were expected to rise about 1.5 million barrels, the survey showed, taking a seasonal back seat to the rest of the report's pieces.
